role: Son of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) and Fatima (RA)
Martyred at the Battle of Karbala
summary: Husayn ibn Ali (RA) was the younger grandson of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through Fatima (RA) and Ali (RA), and among the most beloved members of the Ahl al-Bayt. He was born in Madinah in 4 AH and lived as a companion of the Prophet ﷺ. After the death of his brother Hasan (RA) and in the context of disputes over the caliphate following Muawiyah's death, Husayn was killed at the Battle of Karbala in 61 AH along with members of his family. His martyrdom is mourned by Muslims across traditions and is a defining event in Islamic history.
biography:
Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Hashimi al-Qurashi was born in Madinah in Sha'ban 4 AH (approximately 625 CE), the second son of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) and Fatima bint Muhammad (RA). Like his brother Hasan, the Prophet ﷺ called the adhan in his ear at birth and named him Husayn — a diminutive form paired with Hasan, both names being coined by the Prophet ﷺ himself, as Ibn Sa'd records in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (Vol. 3). The Prophet ﷺ was seen on numerous occasions carrying Husayn on his back, kissing him, and publicly expressing his love for him. He declared: 'Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn. Allah loves whoever loves Husayn.' (Sunan Ibn Majah, Kitab al-Muqaddimah — graded hasan sahih). Both Hasan and Husayn were described by the Prophet ﷺ as 'the leaders of the youth of Paradise' (Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Manaqib).

Husayn was a child when the Prophet ﷺ died in 11 AH, and like his brother he is counted as a companion (Sahabi) by virtue of having seen, heard, and been in the company of the Prophet ﷺ. He narrated hadith from both his grandfather, his mother Fatima, his father Ali, and from the major companions. During the caliphates of Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman (RA), Husayn lived in Madinah and participated in military campaigns. He fought alongside his father Ali (RA) at the Battle of the Camel and the Battle of Siffin.

After the abdication of his brother Hasan and during the caliphate of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, Husayn lived in Madinah without active political opposition. This period is well-documented by classical historians including al-Dhahabi and al-Tabari. When Muawiyah died in 60 AH and his son Yazid ibn Muawiyah assumed the caliphate, the political dynamics shifted. Yazid demanded that Husayn give bay'ah (oath of allegiance) to him. Husayn declined, considering Yazid unfit for the caliphate, and departed from Madinah for Makkah. He then received numerous letters and delegations from the people of Kufah urging him to come to Iraq and lead them against Yazid's authority. Against the advice of several senior companions and relatives — including Ibn Abbas (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA), who counseled him strongly not to go — Husayn proceeded toward Kufah with a small group of family and companions.

On his way to Kufah, Husayn received the devastating news that his emissary to Kufah, Muslim ibn Aqil, had been killed and the people of Kufah had abandoned their pledges of support under pressure from Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, the governor of Kufah and Basra. Despite this, Husayn continued. His caravan was intercepted by the forces of Ibn Ziyad at a plain near the Euphrates River, in the area known as Karbala, on the second of Muharram 61 AH (October 680 CE). After several days of negotiations broke down and the water supply to Husayn's camp was cut off, a battle took place on the tenth of Muharram — the day subsequently known as Ashura — on 10 Muharram 61 AH.

Husayn ibn Ali (RA) was killed in the battle along with most of the male members of his party, including several of his brothers, sons, and nephews. Al-Tabari's detailed account in Tarikh al-Rusul wal-Muluk (Vol. 5) and Ibn Sa'd's account in al-Tabaqat (Vol. 6) are the primary classical historical records. The survivors, including Husayn's son Ali ibn Husayn (later known as Zayn al-Abidin) and several women of the family, were taken as captives to Kufah and then to Damascus.

The killing of Husayn (RA) was condemned by the companions and their successors. In Sunni classical tradition, the events of Karbala are understood as a political and historical tragedy, not as a theological axis. Husayn (RA) is honored as a martyr of the highest rank, as a member of the Ahl al-Bayt whom the Prophet ﷺ loved intensely, and as one who stood by his principles at the cost of his life. The companions and their successors mourned him while not adopting the specific theological and ritual practices that developed in later Shia tradition around the commemoration of Karbala. Classical Sunni scholars are uniform in condemning his killing as an act of injustice while refraining from the sectarian theological frameworks that developed later.

Husayn ibn Ali (RA) was approximately 56 years old at the time of his martyrdom. He is buried at Karbala, where his grave became a site of historical significance. Al-Dhahabi, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Sa'd all record his death with grief and unambiguous condemnation of those responsible.

key_events.event: Born in Madinah; Prophet ﷺ called adhan, named him Husayn
Death of the Prophet ﷺ — Husayn was approximately 6-7 years old
Fought alongside his father Ali (RA) at the Battle of the Camel
Fought alongside his father Ali (RA) at the Battle of Siffin
Refused bay'ah to Yazid ibn Muawiyah; departed Madinah for Makkah
Traveled toward Kufah after receiving letters from its people; his convoy was intercepted at Karbala
Martyred on 10 Muharram 61 AH at the Battle of Karbala; buried there

notable_traits: Physically resembled the Prophet ﷺ — al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi record this
Profound courage and willingness to stand by principle regardless of consequence
Deeply compassionate toward the poor and those in need
Continued the scholarly and spiritual legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt after his brother Hasan (RA)
Prophet's ﷺ intense love for him is documented in multiple authenticated narrations
